raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #60391. When one rank has a usable AOT artifact and another does not, each rank currently makes its own load-or-compile decision, so the ranks split: loaded ranks run a model whose collectives the compiling ranks never join, and under `VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD` the failing rank dies while its peers hang in a later collective. This PR makes the decision collective: every rank loads iff every rank has a usable artifact.

## Claims

- The AOT load-or-compile decision is now uniform across all ranks of a multi-rank run: any rank missing its artifact, or failing to load it, sends every rank down the compile path.
- Under `VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD`, a load failure now raises on every rank instead of killing one rank and hanging the rest.
- Single-rank runs and runs without an initialized process group keep the exact previous behavior.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py` spawn two gloo ranks sharing one cache root; rank 1 deletes its artifact between phases, and each rank records its load attempts and outcomes for the parent to assert on:

- `test_aot_load_decision_is_uniform_across_ranks`: phase B (rank 1 lost its artifact) makes **zero** load attempts on either rank, where the old code let rank 0 attempt (and here fail) its own load; phase C (artifacts re-saved) has both ranks attempt the load together with a uniform outcome.
- `test_force_aot_load_fails_uniformly_across_ranks`: with `VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD=1`, the missing artifact raises `RuntimeError` on **both** ranks instead of one.

Commands and results (macOS, torch 2.13.0, Python 3.14, CPU):

```
python -m pytest tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py::test_aot_load_decision_is_uniform_across_ranks \
                 tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py::test_force_aot_load_fails_uniformly_across_ranks -q
# 2 passed in 14.38s
```

Red-green check: with `vllm/compilation/decorators.py` stashed, `test_aot_load_decision_is_uniform_across_ranks` fails on the load-attempt assertions; with the change it passes.

Full file: `python -m pytest tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py` gives 5 failed, 21 passed, 2 skipped, 1 error. The 5 failures and the error reproduce identically on unmodified upstream/main in this environment (`test_save_and_load` and siblings fail here on a torch-side `'function' object has no attribute 'finalize_loading'` load error, plus one WorkerProc startup issue); they are macOS/torch-2.13 environment limitations, not regressions from this change. The two new tests are part of the 21 passed.

## Details

Root cause: the load decision at the `@support_torch_compile` call site was purely local (`_try_load_aot_compiled_fn` per rank). The issue reporter hit this on the TPU plugin path, where a healthy rank loaded its artifact while an unhealthy rank compiled, and the two model variants diverged on collective usage.

Design: `_load_aot_fn_uniform` wraps the existing loader with two `all_gather_object` checkpoints when `world_size > 1`:

1. Artifact presence (file exists and is non-empty). Any rank without one sends every rank to compile.
2. Load success. A rank whose load raised reports the failure to the gather instead of raising past it, so no peer blocks in the collective; any disagreement sends every rank to compile, and `VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD` re-raises uniformly on all ranks.

Both checkpoints are unconditional and in the same order on every rank, so the gather itself cannot introduce a new split. Tradeoff: multi-rank runs now compile on all ranks when previously the healthy ranks could have loaded, which is strictly the safe direction (compile is always correct) and matches how the rest of the compilation cache already treats rank divergence.

Limitations: validated on 2-process gloo/CPU; I do not have TPU or multi-GPU hardware here, so the CUDA and TPU plugin paths were not run. The collective used is plain `all_gather_object` on the default process group, the same mechanism vLLM already relies on elsewhere for cross-rank coordination.

Duplicate check: no open PR references #60391; the only issue comment is my own claim. AI assistance was used in the preparation of this PR; every changed line was reviewed and the tests above were run by the human submitter.

nodes.body:
Thanks for picking this up. The two gathers cover the missing, truncated and failed-to-load cases from #60391.

It looks like a rank can still end up waiting alone when not every rank in the default process group runs the same compiled modules. The gathers are on the default group, so every rank in it has to call `_load_aot_fn_uniform` the same number of times. With pipeline parallelism plus speculative decoding, the drafter is only built on the last PP rank (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` line 604, `if self.speculative_config and get_pp_group().is_last_rank:`; and `if self.is_last_pp_rank:` at line 290 of `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`; line numbers at the PR head), and drafter models such as `llama_eagle3.LlamaModel` are `@support_torch_compile`. So with PP=2 + EAGLE3 and AOT compile on (the default on torch >= 2.10), the last PP rank would enter the first `all_gather_object` for the drafter, PP rank 0 never would, and the last rank would wait until the process-group timeout and then raise. The first gather runs whether or not an artifact exists, so this would happen on every start, cold cache included.

I have not run PP + EAGLE on this branch; the above is from reading the code. I did check the gather on its own: `_load_aot_fn_uniform` copied verbatim, two gloo ranks, the loader stubbed to succeed, both ranks call it once for the target, then only rank 1 calls it again for a drafter while rank 0 keeps running. Rank 1 blocks for the full timeout (15 s in the test) and raises `RuntimeError: ... Timed out waiting 15000ms`.

<details>
<summary>script</summary>

```python
# _load_aot_fn_uniform copied from vllm/compilation/decorators.py at 746e5facc9 into uniform_fn.py
import datetime, logging, os, tempfile, time, types
import torch, torch.distributed as dist, torch.multiprocessing as mp

def worker(rank, port, d):
    dist.init_process_group("gloo", init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}", rank=rank,
                            world_size=2, timeout=datetime.timedelta(seconds=15))
    g = {"torch": torch, "os": os, "Any": object, "logger": logging.getLogger("x"),
         "envs": types.SimpleNamespace(VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD=False),
         "_try_load_aot_compiled_fn": lambda m, p: object()}
    exec(open("uniform_fn.py").read(), g)
    for name in ["target"] + (["drafter"] if rank == 1 else []):  # drafter only on the last PP rank
        p = os.path.join(d, f"{name}_rank{rank}"); open(p, "wb").write(b"x")
        try:
            g["_load_aot_fn_uniform"](None, p); print(f"rank{rank} {name}: ok", flush=True)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"rank{rank} {name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}", flush=True)
    if rank == 0:
        time.sleep(40)  # rank 0 keeps serving and never reaches the drafter gather

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mp.spawn(worker, args=(29571, tempfile.mkdtemp()), nprocs=2, join=True)
```

Output: `rank0 target: ok`, `rank1 target: ok`, then after 15 s `rank1 drafter: RuntimeError: [...gloo...] Timed out waiting 15000ms ...`.
</details>

One way out would be to gather over the ranks that actually build and run the module, for example the TP group of the current PP stage, rather than the whole world.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@@ -2,8 +2,10 @@
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 
 import hashlib
+import json
 import os
 import pickle
+import shutil
 import tempfile
 from contextlib import contextmanager
 from pathlib import Path
@@ -15,6 +17,7 @@
 import vllm.envs as envs
 import vllm.kernels  # noqa: F401 to register kernels
 from vllm import ir
+from vllm.compilation import decorators as compile_decorators
 from vllm.compilation.backends import VllmBackend
 from vllm.compilation.caching import (
     StandaloneCompiledArtifacts,
@@ -25,6 +28,7 @@
 from vllm.config import (
     CompilationConfig,
     CompilationMode,
+    ParallelConfig,
     VllmConfig,
     set_current_vllm_config,
 )
@@ -35,7 +39,7 @@
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 from vllm.utils.torch_utils import is_torch_equal_or_newer
 
-from ..utils import create_new_process_for_each_test
+from ..utils import create_new_process_for_each_test, get_open_port
 
 
 @pytest.fixture
@@ -192,6 +196,124 @@ def test_save_and_load(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
             assert torch.allclose(ret, expected)
 
 
+def _uniform_aot_load_worker(
+    rank: int, port: int, cache_root: str, force: bool
+) -> None:
+    """Two gloo ranks share a cache root; rank 1 loses its artifact on restart."""
+    torch.distributed.init_process_group(
+        "gloo",
+        init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}",
+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=2,
+    )
+    try:
+        os.environ["VLLM_CACHE_ROOT"] = cache_root
+        os.environ["VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE"] = "1"
+        os.environ["VLLM_USE_MEGA_AOT_ARTIFACT"] = "1"
+        os.environ["VLLM_USE_STANDALONE_COMPILE"] = "1"
+        disable_envs_cache()
+        args = (torch.randn(10, 10),)
+
+        # Spy on the load attempt itself: the uniform gate must skip it
+        # entirely when any rank lacks a usable artifact, not just fail it.
+        real_try_load = compile_decorators._try_load_aot_compiled_fn
+        attempts = {"n": 0}
+
+        def counting_try_load(*a, **k):
+            attempts["n"] += 1
+            return real_try_load(*a, **k)
+
+        compile_decorators._try_load_aot_compiled_fn = counting_try_load
+
+        def fresh_run() -> CompiledMod:
+            vllm_config = VllmConfig(
+                parallel_config=ParallelConfig(rank=rank),
+                compilation_config=CompilationConfig(
+                    mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE,
+                    backend="inductor",
+                ),
+            )
+            with use_vllm_config(vllm_config):
+                mod = CompiledMod(vllm_config=vllm_config)
+                mod(*args)
+            return mod
+
+        def run_and_count() -> tuple[bool, int]:
+            before = attempts["n"]
+            loaded = fresh_run().was_aot_compile_fn_loaded_from_disk
+            return loaded, attempts["n"] - before
+
+        # Phase A: both ranks compile and save their artifacts.
+        outcomes = {}
+        outcomes["a_loaded"], outcomes["a_attempts"] = run_and_count()
+        rank_dirs = list(
+            Path(cache_root).glob(
+                f"torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/*/rank_{rank}_0"
+            )
+        )
+        assert rank_dirs and (rank_dirs[0] / "model").is_file()
+        disable_envs_cache()
+
+        if rank == 1:
+            shutil.rmtree(rank_dirs[0])
+
+        if force:
+            os.environ["VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD"] = "1"
+            disable_envs_cache()
+            with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD"):
+                fresh_run()
+            return
+
+        # Phase B: rank 1 lost its artifact. The load decision is collective,
+        # so both ranks must take the compile path, not just the rank that
+        # lost it. Phase C then sees a uniform decision again once both
+        # artifacts are re-saved (load where the local torch supports it;
+        # success of the load itself is test_save_and_load's contract).
+        outcomes["b_loaded"], outcomes["b_attempts"] = run_and_count()
+        disable_envs_cache()
+        outcomes["c_loaded"], outcomes["c_attempts"] = run_and_count()
+        Path(cache_root, f"outcome_{rank}.json").write_text(json.dumps(outcomes))
+    finally:
+        torch.distributed.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_torch_equal_or_newer("2.10.0"), reason="requires torch 2.10")
+def test_aot_load_decision_is_uniform_across_ranks(tmp_path: Path):
+    """A rank missing its artifact sends every rank to the compile path."""
+    torch.multiprocessing.spawn(
+        _uniform_aot_load_worker,
+        args=(get_open_port(), str(tmp_path), False),
+        nprocs=2,
+        join=True,
+    )
+    rank0, rank1 = (
+        json.loads((tmp_path / f"outcome_{rank}.json").read_text()) for rank in (0, 1)
+    )
+    # No artifacts exist yet: the existence gate sends both ranks to the
+    # compile path without any load attempt.
+    assert rank0["a_loaded"] is False and rank1["a_loaded"] is False
+    assert rank0["a_attempts"] == 0 and rank1["a_attempts"] == 0
+    # Rank 1 lost its artifact: still no load attempt anywhere; a per-rank
+    # gate would have let rank 0 try (and here fail) its own load.
+    assert rank0["b_loaded"] is False and rank1["b_loaded"] is False
+    assert rank0["b_attempts"] == 0 and rank1["b_attempts"] == 0
+    # Artifacts re-saved: both ranks attempt the load together, and whether
+    # it succeeds or not the outcome stays uniform across ranks.
+    assert rank0["c_attempts"] == 1 and rank1["c_attempts"] == 1
+    assert rank0["c_loaded"] == rank1["c_loaded"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_torch_equal_or_newer("2.10.0"), reason="requires torch 2.10")
+def test_force_aot_load_fails_uniformly_across_ranks(tmp_path: Path):
+    """FORCE raises on every rank, not just the rank missing the artifact."""
+    torch.multiprocessing.spawn(
+        _uniform_aot_load_worker,
+        args=(get_open_port(), str(tmp_path), True),
+        nprocs=2,
+        join=True,
+    )
+
+
 @pytest.mark.skipif(
     not current_platform.is_cuda() or not is_torch_equal_or_newer("2.10.0"),
     reason="requires CUDA and torch 2.10",

@@ -341,6 +341,74 @@ def _try_load_aot_compiled_fn(
         return None
 
 
+def _load_aot_fn_uniform(model: Any, aot_compilation_path: str) -> Any | None:
+    """Load the AOT-compiled function, keeping the decision uniform across ranks.
+
+    A rank that compiles while its peers run loaded artifacts can issue
+    collectives the others never join (#60391), so when the model runs on
+    more than one rank the load-or-compile decision is made collectively:
+    every rank loads iff every rank has a usable artifact, and any
+    disagreement sends every rank to the compile path. Under
+    ``VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD`` a failure raises on every rank instead of one
+    rank dying while its peers hang in a later collective.
+    """
+    if not (
+        torch.distributed.is_available()
+        and torch.distributed.is_initialized()
+        and torch.distributed.get_world_size() > 1
+    ):
+        return _try_load_aot_compiled_fn(model, aot_compilation_path)
+
+    world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size()
+
+    def every_rank(ok: bool) -> bool:
+        reports: list[bool] = [False] * world_size
+        torch.distributed.all_gather_object(reports, ok)
+        return all(reports)
+
+    has_artifact = (
+        os.path.isfile(aot_compilation_path)
+        and os.path.getsize(aot_compilation_path) > 0
+    )
+    if not every_rank(has_artifact):
+        reason = "an AOT artifact is missing or empty on at least one rank"
+        if envs.VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD is set but {reason}; "
+                "failing uniformly on all ranks"
+            )
+        logger.warning(
+            "Compiling model again on every rank because %s; a per-rank "
+            "decision could split collective usage across ranks",
+            reason,
+        )
+        return None
+
+    load_error: Exception | None = None
+    try:
+        loaded_fn = _try_load_aot_compiled_fn(model, aot_compilation_path)
+    except Exception as e:
+        # Report the failure to the gather instead of raising past it, so no
+        # peer blocks forever; FORCE re-raises uniformly below.
+        loaded_fn, load_error = None, e
+    if every_rank(loaded_fn is not None):
+        return loaded_fn
+    if envs.VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD:
+        if load_error is not None:
+            raise load_error
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD is set but an AOT artifact failed to load "
+            "on at least one rank; failing uniformly on all ranks"
+        )
+    if load_error is None:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Compiling model again on every rank because an AOT artifact "
+            "failed to load on at least one rank; a per-rank decision could "
+            "split collective usage across ranks",
+        )
+    return None
+
+
 def _support_torch_compile(
     cls: type[_T],
     dynamic_arg_dims: DynamicArgDims,
@@ -584,7 +652,7 @@ def __call__(self: type[_T], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
             cache_dir = os.path.join(cache_dir, f"rank_{rank}_{dp_rank}")
             aot_compilation_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "model")
             if not envs.VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE:
-                loaded_fn = _try_load_aot_compiled_fn(self, aot_compilation_path)
+                loaded_fn = _load_aot_fn_uniform(self, aot_compilation_path)
                 if loaded_fn is not None:
                     self.aot_compiled_fn = loaded_fn
                     self.was_aot_compile_fn_loaded_from_disk = True

Output: `rank0 target: ok`, `rank1 target: ok`, then after 15 s `rank1 drafter: RuntimeError: [...gloo...] Timed out waiting 15000ms ...`.
</details>

One way out would be to gather over the ranks that actually build and run the module, for example the TP group of the current PP stage, rather than the whole world.
